extracted text: The paper focuses on the effect of retrogression and re-aging (RRA) treatment on AA7050 and AA7150 aluminum alloys. The alloys were tested in their original conditions (T77511 for AA7150 and T76511 for AA7050), after T6 treatment (solution heat treated at 475°C for 40 min, water quenched and aged at 120°C for 24 h), and after RRA treatment with retrogression times of 20 and 40 min at 200°C followed by re-aging at 120°C for 24 h. The RRA treatment aims to combine the high strength of T6 condition with the stress corrosion cracking (SCC) resistance of T7 condition. The paper mentions that the microstructure resulting from RRA is a very fine distribution of η′ MgZn₂ in the aluminum matrix grains and η MgZn₂ precipitates on grain boundaries. No specific alloy composition is provided in the paper.
